summary: Recorded the source analysis behind the registered propagation question, so it is self-contained and its readings are separated. The interpretation is source-only with no defect judgment: on the receiving side installSnapshot decodes the request's configuration and index, installs them into latest and committed, sets lastApplied and lastSnapshot to the request's last log index and term and compacts below it (raft.go:1880-1975), after which the follower keeps receiving entries above the snapshot index and processConfigurationLogEntry updates the tracked configuration for any configuration entry in that range (raft.go:1595-1620) - which supports the transient reading. The persistent reading has a concrete path rather than a hypothetical one: a node whose tracked committed configuration is stale writes exactly that configuration into any snapshot it takes afterwards, since takeSnapshot passes the tracked committed configuration and index to SnapshotStore.Create (snapshot.go:155-190), so if such a node leads and snapshots again, the corrective entry - the removal its log still holds - lies below the new snapshot's index and a joiner installing it receives no entry above that would correct it, while compaction retains only trailing logs above the snapshot index. Counterevidence records that the persistent path requires that further snapshot and that the account infers from code rather than observing a joiner, and the limitations mark it as source-only with the trimming interaction unexamined. The question stays open with its discriminator; the run's two defect accounts and their receipts are unchanged.
